clue.text: Go into school to get lines

indicators.note: into says the first piece is put inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: to go, informally, is to urinate, to pee

explanation.surface: A newcomer joins a school to be given lines to learn, or lines as punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a plain verb of motion but is the informal sense of relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's lines are the words of the part, the spoken text delivered on stage.

clue.text: Somewhere to go in Kent, say, to find addict

indicators.note: in means the place to go sits inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: Kent is an example of a county in the South East of England, SE
a lav, a lavatory, is somewhere to go to the toilet

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for a drug user in the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England, so it exemplifies SE.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict is in thrall to a habit, just as people are called a slave to drink or fashion.

clue.text: Trap Poles smuggled over into heart of Greece

indicators.note: into means the poles and the turned word go inside the centre letters
heart of means the central letters of Greece

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: over means the word for smuggled is read backwards

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, so ran means smuggled

explanation.surface: A sting to catch Polish smugglers sneaking into central Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but means the magnetic poles. 'over' turns RAN into NAR; 'heart of' gives EE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to catch in a snare, so it means to trap.

clue.text: Privates and sentry occasionally cross

parts.note: privates are the genitals, the crotch area

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters, here every other one, of sentry are taken

explanation.surface: Soldiers of the lowest rank and a guard sometimes cross a border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privates' look like soldiers but are the body's private parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross as an adjective means bad-tempered, the same as grumpy and irritable.

clue.text: Camera's calibrated to catch villain

indicators.note: to catch means the phrase holds the answer inside it, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A camera has been set up precisely to photograph a criminal in the act.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain and a scoundrel are near synonyms for a wicked or dishonest person.

clue.text: Mimic's job, one for each play finally

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing
per means for each, as in miles per hour

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of play is taken

explanation.surface: An impressionist's work: one turn per show at the end of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Aping is imitation, so this is the practice of copying others, the mimic's trade.

clue.text: Osric once (I think) displays vanity

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Osric, the foppish courtier in Hamlet, shows off his vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: Osric is the affected courtier in Hamlet, a fitting owner for vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceit and vanity are synonyms for an excessive pride in oneself.

clue.text: Left city celeb, American, debauched

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
a celebrity can be idolised as a hero
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: An American celebrity left town after a debauched spell.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postcode for the City, the financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A debauched person indulges in sensual excess, and lechery is lustful excess.

clue.text: I hand down clothes for sort of play

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the phrase wraps round the letter like a garment

parts.note: to hand down is to pass on to someone else

explanation.surface: Someone gives away old clothes to a theatre company for costumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb, not the garments being handed down.
explanation.definitionFit: A Passion play dramatises the suffering and death of Christ, as at Oberammergau.

clue.text: Create cast to tour north and perform again

indicators.note: to tour means to go round, so the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation
cast here means thrown into a new shape, so the letters of create are rearranged

explanation.surface: A director assembles a company to take a show round the north and stage it again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a theatre company but signals the anagram, giving REEACT, which goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enact something is to act it out once more, as historical societies stage old battles.

clue.text: Puzzles turned up to occupy fools

indicators.note: to occupy means to sit inside, so turned up goes within the word for fools

parts.note: to con someone is to fool them
something that turned up was found

explanation.surface: Puzzles have been discovered keeping idiots busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fools' looks like a noun (idiots) but is a verb, meaning cons.
explanation.definitionFit: To puzzle someone is to baffle or bewilder them, to leave them perplexed.

clue.text: Glum local hymn played with energy

indicators.note: played means the letters are performed in a new arrangement

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sad local hymn is sung with gusto, an odd mismatch of mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Glum and gloomy, sorrowful or dejected are close synonyms for low spirits.

clue.text: European certainly has views

parts.note: certainly is an emphatic yes

explanation.surface: A European is sure to hold opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'views' looks like a plural noun (opinions) but is a verb meaning looks at.
explanation.definitionFit: To view something is to look at it, and to eye it is to watch it closely.

clue.text: Part of act speaker's observed

indicators.note: speaker's means what the word sounds like when spoken out

parts.note: observed means seen, which is pronounced exactly like the answer

explanation.surface: An actor's section of the play is noticed by the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays divide into acts and each act into smaller units of action set in one place.

clue.text: Small children jumped, talked and moved with effort

indicators.note: talked means the word is spelt the way it sounds in speech

parts.note: jumped means leaped, often said with a short vowel

explanation.surface: Young children leapt about and chattered while trudging along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumped' is spelt by its sound, LEPPED, as in Irish dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Schlep, from Yiddish, means to haul or trudge with effort, so this is moved laboriously.

clue.text: Amusing exploit without a purpose

parts.note: amusing means fun, used as an adjective

indicators.note: without means the following letter is taken out of the word for exploit

parts.note: an exploit is an action or deed

explanation.surface: A pointless prank: an entertaining stunt with no real aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A from ACTION, giving CTION.
explanation.definitionFit: The function of a thing is its role or the use it is meant to serve.

clue.text: Plea in court when match is abandoned

definitions.meaning: a defendant's formal plea of neither admitting nor denying a charge
a bout declared void, as when one side cannot continue

explanation.definitionFit: Nolo contendere is a plea in law, and a boxing or sporting bout can be declared void.

clue.text: Reply to gift of tissue during short trip

indicators.note: during means the second piece sits within the shortened trip
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a trip or journey is a tour
a tissue is a hanky, a handkerchief

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledges a present of tissues on a brief holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reply to gift' is the whole definition; 'of' merely links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'thanks' is the standard grateful response when handed a present.

clue.text: Love recording absorbing Beethoven's Fifth

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the picked letter goes inside

parts.note: recording something is noting it down

indicators.note: fifth means the fifth letter of the composer's name, not his symphony

explanation.surface: A beloved recording of Beethoven's Fifth Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is the tennis term for a zero score. 'Beethoven's Fifth' is not the symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, love means a score of zero, which is nil.

clue.text: Wraps carbon copies

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
to ape is to copy or imitate

explanation.surface: An office instruction to bundle up carbon copies of documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carbon copies' reads as one office item, but the words split: carbon gives C, copies is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Capes are sleeveless outer garments wrapped round the shoulders, so wraps as a noun.

clue.text: Game hard going for field worker

indicators.note: going means the letter for hard disappears from the game bird

parts.note: pheasant is a game bird
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A game that is hard going for a farm labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like a sport but is shot game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a small farmer or farm labourer working the land.

clue.text: Guys hold this view: tablet has been nicked

indicators.note: has been nicked means a piece has been stolen from the word for view

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or view held
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Men believe a certain opinion, and a stone tablet has been stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' are not men but guy ropes, which hold a canvas shelter up.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy ropes are the lines that keep a camping shelter's canvas taut and upright.

clue.text: Superfluity embarrassed duke in posh French city

parts.note: embarrassed people go red in the face
U means upper-class, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

indicators.note: in means the duke's abbreviation goes inside the following letters

parts.note: Nancy is a city in Lorraine, north-eastern France

explanation.surface: A duke feels awkward finding himself in an upmarket French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Superfluity is excess beyond what is needed, the state of being surplus to requirements.

clue.text: Four rake round top of garden

definitions.note: refers to the entry at 4-across, the villain, whose synonym this is

indicators.note: round means the rake surrounds the picked letter

parts.note: a roue is a rake, a dissolute man

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of garden

explanation.surface: Four gardening rakes are put round the top of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four' is a cross-reference to 4-across, the villain; 'rake' looks like a garden tool but is a libertine.
explanation.definitionFit: The 4-across answer and a knave or scoundrel are synonyms for a dishonest person.

clue.text: Pick up this clue for Heller work

definitions.meaning: to pick up is to seize or grab something
this is 22-down, and Joseph Heller's novel is the word plus 22

explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Heller wrote the novel 'Catch-22'; this clue is numbered 22.
explanation.definitionFit: Picking up a thrown object is to grab it, and Heller's war novel adds 22 to this word.

clue.text: Call in agent to supply elastic

indicators.note: in means the call goes inside the word for agent

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: Phoning a commercial agent to order a supply of elastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic bounces back into shape, which is what a resilient, bouncy thing does.

clue.text: Elaborate play with ten might be fine

indicators.note: elaborate is a verb here, working the letters up into something new

explanation.surface: An elaborate game for ten players might turn out well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like an adjective meaning good, but is a noun: a monetary punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine is a punishment paid in money, one kind of sanction for breaking a rule.

clue.text: Like Dirk the German astride a horse

indicators.note: astride means straddling, so the German article goes on either side

parts.note: der is the masculine form of 'the' in German
GG, short for gee-gee, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A man called Dirk is compared to a German riding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirk' looks like a man's name; it is a Scottish short stabbing blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirk is a long Scottish knife, a weapon of the same short-bladed stabbing kind.

clue.text: It could be plain one's naked without one

definitions.meaning: in knitting, plain and purl are the two basic loops made with the needles
having not a single item of clothing on is the idiom for being completely naked

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about something plain whose absence leaves you naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain is a basic knitting loop, and 'without a stitch on' is an idiom for wearing nothing.
